title: Why do golf balls have dimples? And how many are there?

sources.name: Titleist — The purpose of golf-ball dimples
Titleist — 2025 Pro V1 and Pro V1x specifications

practice: See which sporting details you recognise in the Sports Quiz.

sections.title: The dents help it fly
sections.html:
Golf balls have dimples because they change the airflow around the ball, reducing drag and helping it travel farther. A perfectly smooth surface sounds faster. Here, the air disagrees.

The little dents are part of the engineering, rather than decoration or damage from a particularly enthusiastic round.

sections.title: A little turbulence does useful work
sections.html:
Dimples stir up the thin layer of air close to the surface. This helps it stay attached farther around the ball before separating, reducing the pressure drag that slows it down.

NASA explains why that roughness helps. It is not a general rule that scratching anything makes it faster: shape and speed matter too.

sections.title: How many dimples are on a golf ball?
sections.html:
The number depends on the model. For example, Titleist’s published 2025 specifications give:

  • Pro V1: 388 dimples.
  • Pro V1x: 348 dimples.

Those are examples, not a universal answer for every ball. Titleist’s engineers also consider depth, shape and arrangement; a bigger count does not automatically mean better flight.

sections.title: A better question for the next quiz
sections.html:
If someone asks for an exact dimple count, ask which ball they mean. The model is part of the answer.

For another sporting detail hiding in plain sight, discover why tennis balls turned yellow.
